changelog.4: META:<origin> records -- Chrome's own per-origin commit bookkeeping, previously skipped entirely -- are now decoded and reported as their own 'commit_metadata' rows (record_type field distinguishes them from real 'data' rows). A small, fixed 2-field protobuf, decoded with a purpose-built varint reader: field 1 = commit timestamp (Chromium's own base::Time/webkit_us epoch, using this project's existing timestamp_fields unit code), field 2 = committed byte size. Confirmed against CCL Solutions Group's own published research and directly verified byte-by-byte against three real values (dates land in 2024-01/2024-07, before this archive's own July 2024 acquisition; sizes are small and plausible). Also corrected _decode_value's tag=0x01 case from UTF-8 to Latin-1, per the same CCL research -- confirmed zero effect on this archive's own 335 real tag=0x01 values (all pure ASCII, byte-identical under either encoding) but strictly safer (Latin-1 never raises) and matches Chromium's own actual convention.

changelog.2: New parser -- every WiFi network this device has joined, from private/var/preferences/com.apple.wifi.known-networks.plist. Built specifically to exercise artifact_runner.decode_plist_blob against a real, WHOLE plist FILE in a shipped parser (every prior caller only fed it a BLOB column). Modeled on iLEAPP's own appleWifiPlist.py, with two deliberate differences documented in this module's own docstring. Verified against the real IOS17 JoshHickman archive: 17 real network rows, exactly matching iLEAPP's own documented sample_data count for its 'iphone11_ios17' test archive (the same iPhone 11 / iOS 17.3 device) -- a real cross-tool number check, not just 'the code ran'.
changelog.3: Report Notes (description) now documents the real research done on the un-surfaced 'Moving' field, at direct user request following a discussion of it: checked two dedicated public write-ups on this exact plist (neither mentions it), then found a real cross-archive pattern by building .zcd caches for this project's other two real iOS archives -- Moving=True on exactly 2 of 67 real entries total, both SSIDs naming a mobile device's own hotspot (a car, a GoPro camera). Two competing hypotheses (restored via Cloud Sync; iOS WiFi Password Sharing) were tested directly against the same real data and neither held up. Stated as a documented hypothesis for a future re-check, not surfaced as a report column or claimed as fact -- no output/behavior change, description text only.
changelog.5: Added password_modified_at (__OSSpecific__.WiFiNetworkPasswordModificationDate) -- Tier 2/3 addition per direct research discussion: forensafe.com independently names this field for this exact plist (name-corroborated), and this project's own direct check across all 29 real occurrences on two archives found a clean, 100% pattern -- it lands within a fraction of a second of added_at for every locally-added network, and diverges for EVERY SINGLE Cloud-Sync-added one, no exceptions. Held off on the BSSList report (per-access-point geolocation) -- its own field set is iLEAPP-confirmed, but what the Latitude/Longitude actually represent (this device's own position vs. a crowd-sourced AP reference position) is unresolved even in the public forensics community (a Forensic Focus forum thread asks this exact question, unanswered) -- not shipping a location-bearing report on an unverified evidentiary claim.
